title: [BugFix][CUDA][RNG] Reject binding the void rng_init result
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/3243/files) against `main`.

## Summary

`rng_init` is a side-effect-only intrinsic: the curand state is a function-scope
variable owned by the codegen, and the call itself is `void`. The frontend
nevertheless documented a `state : PrimExpr` return, so following the
documented usage produced `void state = ;` in the generated CUDA and an nvcc
`incomplete type "void" is not allowed` error, instead of a TileLang diagnostic.

Reject binding a value-less expression in the eager frontend, naming both the
variable and the offending expression. The CUDA codegen additionally rejects a
bound `rng_init` call as a backstop for paths that bypass the eager builder.

Fixes #3029

## Changes

`tilelang/language/eager/builder.py`
- reject binding a value-less (void) expression in `bind_immutable`. This
  covers `rng_init` and any other side-effecting intrinsic.

`src/cuda/codegen/codegen_cuda.cc` / `.h`
- add `VisitStmt_(const BindNode *op)` as a codegen backstop. `Bind` is this
  tree's name for the let-binding node; the override matches the existing ones
  in `codegen_py.cc` and `codegen_cutedsl.cc` and delegates to
  `CodeGenC::VisitStmt_`, which is the only implementation in the class chain.

`tilelang/cuda/language/random.py`
- the `Returns` docstring now describes the call as a statement whose `void`
  result exists only so the statement reaches the IR.

`testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_rand.py`
- 1 new regression.

## Validation

Environment: NVIDIA L20 (sm_89), CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128,
Python 3.13.14; base `e40e09e3e61595083d63a38bcf67f7ccb976b2ea` (current `main`).
`bash format.sh` passes on every changed file.

### Observable behaviour

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `state = T.rng_init(seed)` | generated `void _state = ;` -> nvcc `incomplete type "void" is not allowed` | frontend `Cannot bind \`_state\` to a value-less expression: ... has void type` |
| bare `T.rng_init(seed)` | compiles and runs | compiles and runs (unchanged) |

The regression accepts either diagnostic, because the frontend now fires first
while the codegen check remains as a backstop; the contract is that malformed
CUDA never reaches nvcc.

### Test results

`testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_rand.py`:

| build | result |
|---|---|
| before (unpatched `main`) | **1 failed, 6 passed** |
| after | **7 passed** |

```text
FAILED test_rand_init_result_cannot_be_bound     # before only
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary

- Reject bindings of value-less expressions in the eager frontend.
- Reject bound `rng_init` calls in CUDA codegen.
- Document `rng_init` as a statement with kernel-owned state.
- Add regression coverage for invalid `rng_init` bindings.
- Preserve bare `T.rng_init(seed)` statements.

## C++ style / lint notes

- The PR changes C++ codegen but does not modify rules documented in `docs/developer_guide/cpp_style.md`.
- CI includes the warning-only **C++ API Style Audit** step.
- No audit findings or test results were supplied.

title: [CUDA][Transform] Lower launch-invariant integer arithmetic
body:
**Near-specialized performance for dynamic shapes, without per-shape recompilation.**

Related issue: https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/3261.

Most of the credit for the real-world improvement belongs to @penguin-wwy. Without the core idea from #3267, this work would not have benefited the real-world cases below. The remainder canonicalization and factor matching substantially follow that implementation; the MoE permutation kernel, reference and shapes also come from its benchmark. Thanks also for the original analysis in #3261.

## Real-operator comparison from #3267

All three of @penguin-wwy's `examples/permute_scales` cases use the original dynamic kernel, reference and shapes, without added assumptions. Shapes `(experts, N, K, group size)` are `(256, 2048, 7168, 32)` for both DSV3 cases and `(8, 4096, 8192, 128)` for Llama4.

RTX 5090, Linux, NVCC 13.2.78. Saved CUDA sources from [#3267 at 087f6aff](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/commit/087f6aff7c922c9b61a9191c5c3d822873bc3775) and this PR at `dd6c9f3b` are compiled with the same options and timed in one process: 31 interleaved rounds, 64 launches per graph, five replays per sample. The table shows the second of two runs with consistent results. Times are median GPU microseconds and exclude host preparation; speedups are medians of per-round paired ratios. Both implementations produce byte-identical Off sources and byte-identical Const sources. These measurements do not reproduce the H200 results.

| Case | Off (µs) | #3267 (µs) | Dynamic, this PR (µs) | Const (µs) | Off / dynamic | #3267 / dynamic | Dynamic / const |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DSV3 W4A16 | 1069.631 | 1065.480 | 978.880 | 971.898 | 1.094× | 1.089× | 1.007× |
| DSV3 W4A8 | 1057.814 | 1049.406 | 984.275 | 975.978 | 1.074× | 1.067× | 1.008× |
| Llama4 W4A16 | 12.753 | 12.337 | 10.873 | 10.334 | 1.171× | 1.134× | 1.051× |

Const fixes the shape at compile time with this pass disabled, while retaining the same kernel body, 256-thread layout and reference. It is an approximate specialization ceiling for this schedule, not a strict performance bound. Dynamic latency is within about 0.9% of Const for the two DSV3 cases and 5.2% for Llama4 in this run. The aim is to approach specialization performance with a reusable dynamic kernel instead of compiling a variant for every shape.

All variants pass exact output comparisons and poisoned-output graph replay checks. Native TVM-FFI runs check Off/on/Const on each implementation; the GPU-only comparison uses their saved CUDA sources.

## Implementation

TileLang adds opt-in `LowerInvariantArithmetic`, enabled with `tl.enable_invariant_arithmetic`. One pass factory exposes two stages: `stage="prepare"` prepares host parameters before `SplitHostDevice`, which captures them as flat kernel arguments; `stage="materialize"` shares device arithmetic after final simplification and restores SSA. The stages communicate through IR.

- Supports scalar signed/unsigned 8-, 16-, 32- and 64-bit arithmetic, including widened index expressions.
- Shares multiplier/shift or Barrett parameters between div/rem and equivalent widened uses.
- Selects reciprocal width from dividend magnitude bounds, rather than divisor storage width. Signed floor/truncating div/rem use unsigned magnitude arithmetic; negative and wide inputs no longer select ordinary-division fallbacks.
- Preserves original-width wrapping in both host preparation and device operands using unsigned intermediates. In particular, `uint64(h * w)` and `uint64(h) * uint64(w)` are not interchangeable, and a wrapped signed swizzle input must retain its sign.
- Eliminates redundant coordinate reconstruction and reuses existing quotient prefixes when positive, non-overflowing divisor products are proven.
- Replaces bounded swizzle remainders with one compare/subtract, without reciprocal preparation. Bounds can come from existing conditions or explicit min/max clamps; the pass does not add assumptions.

Existing conditions, assumptions and range information supply compile-time sign proofs to the device intrinsics, without extra launch arguments. Positive factors only establish a positive product when its range excludes overflow. Eligible unsigned computations stay in 32 bits until the result is widened; identity-divisor results are selected after reciprocal arithmetic to preserve common subexpressions.

Preparation is structurally deduplicated within each device region. Device operations remain intrinsics until CUDA codegen, rather than expanding nested guarded formulas during IR simplification. The pass uses TVM-FFI without adapter changes. C host codegen emits scalar 32/64-bit bit-scan helpers for `clz`, replacing the comparison-sum expansion, with explicit zero handling and a portable fallback. CUDA Graph replay retains capture-time parameters; host preparation runs during capture, not replay.

Late materialization reuses pure arithmetic already evaluated by a dominating condition inside its branches. It does not speculate across lazy guards or reuse mutable loads. Remainder normalization and layout decoding share one traversal, which also recovers remainders split across reassociated swizzle expressions, including missing multiples of an outer power-of-two modulus. This avoids recomputing coordinate quotients without adding assumptions or narrowing indices. Within a single unguarded load address, an existing remainder also replaces its matching quotient product using $qd=x-r$, preserving word width; reuse does not cross lazy expressions or statements.

Launch-extent types provide additional index bounds without preventing device index widening. Sign/range facts are keyed by node identity and retained only when valid at every occurrence. Casts can use proven source bounds, while potentially wrapping arithmetic blocks mathematical sign/range proofs; remainder and bitwise operations can re-establish facts about their results independently of the input range. Runtime assumption checks that depend on local scalar bindings remain after those definitions.

## Arithmetic correctness

### FastDiv / FastRem

For divisor magnitude $1<d\le2^{31}$ and normalized dividend $0\le x\le2^{31}$, define

$$
s=\lfloor\log_2(d-1)\rfloor,\qquad P=2^{32+s},\qquad
m=\left\lceil\frac{P}{d}\right\rceil.
$$

For this divisor range, $m$ fits uint32. Write $md=P+e$ and $x=qd+r$, with $0\le e<d\le2^{s+1}$ and $0\le r<d$. Since $xe<P$,

$$
\frac{xm}{P}=q+\frac{r+xe/P}{d},\qquad
0\le\frac{r+xe/P}{d}<1.
$$

Thus `mulhi32(x, m) >> s` gives $q=\lfloor x/d\rfloor$ exactly, and $r=x-qd$. Since $qd\le x\le2^{31}$, FastRem can compute its magnitude multiply/subtract in uint32 and widen only the result. The $d=1$ result is selected separately.

### Barrett quotient and remainder

Let $B=2^w$, where $w\in\{32,64\}$, $0\le x<B$, and $d>1$. Prepare $\mu=\lfloor B/d\rfloor$ and compute $\widehat q=\lfloor x\mu/B\rfloor$ by high multiplication. Then

$$
0\le\frac{x}{d}-\frac{x\mu}{B}
=\frac{x(B-\mu d)}{Bd}<1.
$$

Therefore $\widehat q$ is either $q$ or $q-1$. The residual $\widehat r=x-\widehat qd$ fits the dividend word, and one correction suffices:

$$
c=\mathbf{1}[\widehat r\ge d],\qquad
q=\widehat q+c,\qquad r=\widehat r-cd.
$$

This also covers a wider divisor: if $d\ge B$, then $\mu\le1$ and the same bound applies. The correction compares against the full-width divisor. Native 64-bit preparation needs no host int128:

$$
\left\lfloor\frac{2^{64}}d\right\rfloor
=\left\lfloor\frac{2^{64}-1}d\right\rfloor
+\mathbf{1}\!\left[(2^{64}-1)\bmod d=d-1\right].
$$

The $d=1$ case is handled separately.

### Signed floor and truncating arithmetic

Magnitudes $A=|x|$ and $D=|d|$ are computed with unsigned arithmetic, including the signed minimum. For truncation, divide $A$ by $D$ and restore the quotient sign from both operands and the remainder sign from $x$.

For floor division, define

$$
b=\mathbf{1}[(x<0)\ne(d<0)\ \land\ A\ne0],\qquad
A-b=qD+r,\qquad 0\le r<D.
$$

The quotient magnitude is $q+b$. The remainder magnitude is $r$ when $b=0$, otherwise $D-1-r$, with the divisor's sign. This follows from $A=qD+r+1$ in the opposite-sign case. A positive-divisor specialization uses bitwise complement to normalize negative dividends without per-lane fallback branches. Unsigned operands omit sign restoration.

Only a zero divisor retains the original fallback; a nonzero proof removes it. Division by zero and the unrepresentable signed minimum divided by $-1$ are outside the correctness claim.

### Layout decoding and bounded swizzles

For positive $a,b$ with a non-overflowing product, let $q=\lfloor x/a\rfloor$. Then

$$
\left\lfloor\frac{x}{ab}\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac{q}{b}\right\rfloor,\qquad
\left\lfloor\frac{x}{ab}\right\rfloor b+(q\bmod b)=q.
$$

This removes redundant coordinate reconstruction, including for negative $x$. Quotient factorization is applied only when the corresponding prefix already occurs. Products that may wrap are left unfactored.

For $0\le r,m<d$, the swizzled index satisfies $r\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}m\le r+m<2d$; bitwise OR obeys the same bound. Its remainder therefore needs only one conditional subtraction. The bound is proved without evaluating an overflowing $2d$. Offline BitVec tests check the single-correction identity and XOR/OR bounds over 8-, 16-, 32- and 64-bit domains.


For reassociated expressions, let $x=t+a$, $q=\lfloor x/d\rfloor$ and $r=x-qd$. If $M=2^k$ and $M\mid a$, then

$$
(t-qd)\bmod M=(r-a)\bmod M=r\bmod M.
$$

This remains valid under $w$-bit wrapping when $k\le w$, since $M\mid2^w$. TileLang restores an omitted term only after proving its divisibility by $M$, without distributing products or crossing casts. Non-power-of-two outer moduli do not use this rule.

## Real-operator host-wall comparison

Native TVM-FFI measurements below include host preparation and synchronization, excluding compilation; 21 interleaved rounds. This is a separate Off/on/Const comparison, not a host-overhead comparison with #3267.

| Case | Wall Off (µs) | Wall dynamic (µs) | Wall Const (µs) | Off / dynamic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DSV3 W4A16 | 1066.627 | 968.567 | 970.937 | 1.101× |
| DSV3 W4A8 | 1055.693 | 976.457 | 977.349 | 1.081× |
| Llama4 W4A16 | 13.692 | 12.506 | 12.502 | 1.095× |

### Host preparation ablation

Replacing the C host `clz` expansion leaves device sources unchanged. In two complete old/new ablations (31 interleaved rounds each), positive-parameter gather measures 1.039× wall speedup at 4,096 elements and 1.031–1.044× at 1,048,576 elements. The three real MoE cases show no meaningful end-to-end change from this host-only adjustment.

An isolated scalar FastDiv-preparation benchmark measures 16.20 ns with the comparison sum and 3.74 ns with bit scanning (4.33×); this is parameter-preparation cost, not kernel or end-to-end speedup.

## Representative results

Same GPU and toolchain, TVM-FFI. Medians of 11 interleaved rounds, 256 launches per sample. GPU time uses CUDA graphs; wall time includes host preparation and synchronization, excluding compilation.

**Off** disables the optimization; **Lower** enables host-prepared arithmetic; **Late** additionally enables late device materialization. Lower and Late have identical host code. Speedups compare Off with Late.

### 1,048,576 elements

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| Swizzled, pitched gather | 13.720 | 12.036 | 7.137 | 1.92× | 14.491 | 14.400 | 8.279 | 1.75× |

The original gather has no added assumptions. The four additional variants use `h,w,c != 0`, `h,w,c > 0`, `0 < h,w,c <= 1024`, and uint32 parameters with nonzero assumptions, respectively. The bounded variant also establishes non-overflowing divisor products. The bounded-swizzle variant additionally assumes `c >= 32`. title: [CUDA] Fuse exact FP4 to FP8 conversion through FP32
body:
## Motivation

The [DeepSeek V4.1 expert GEMM](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/kernel.py#L477-L559) converts E2M1 weights through FP32 into E4M3 on every K tile. Every E2M1 value, including signed zero, has an exact E4M3 encoding.

## Implementation

I fuse this unannotated CUDA cast chain into two `__byte_perm` operations per four elements. The code handles scalars and vector widths 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32. Explicit cast annotations retain their existing lowering. The conversion uses registers and adds no global or shared-memory allocation.

## Validation

- Native source-generation tests cover both E4M3 dtype spellings, all supported widths, and explicit annotations.
- The [upstream H100 job](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/actions/runs/34607356388/job/103289438636) passed the source-generation cases and all four exhaustive PyTorch runtime cases. Each runtime case checks every packed four-nibble word against an independent encoding table. The subsequent helper rename preserves the generated CUDA operations; the renamed source-generation cases and CUDA compilation pass.
- The extracted GEMM produces identical BF16 outputs in every configuration below. An independent sampled CPU reference also passes.
- Project hooks pass for all three contribution files. Current-head CUDA, ROCm, Metal, and CuTeDSL CI checks pass.

## H100 performance

The benchmark uses the linked GEMM with `T.symbolic` adapted to `T.dynamic`: 128 threads, tiles of 32 by 128 by 32, two pipeline stages, 10,240 bytes of shared memory, FP32 accumulation, and BF16 output. The consumer pins TileLang 0.1.8; the benchmark uses compiler `c629fe5e` and this patch. Baseline CUDA source matches the unmodified compiler's output.

Both variants run on the same H100 80 GB HBM3 with CUDA 13.0, targeting `sm_90a`, and use identical inputs and power-of-two scales. Each graph contains 100 calls. Values are per-call medians from ten retained alternating-order CUDA-event measurements after warmup.

| M | N | K | Baseline (µs) | This PR (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2,304 | 5,120 | 547.94 | 108.65 |
| 8 | 2,304 | 5,120 | 549.32 | 108.59 |
| 32 | 2,304 | 5,120 | 550.15 | 111.02 |

title: [BugFix][CUDA][RNG] Derive the default rng_init sequence from the full launch
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/3242/files) against `main`.

## Summary

`rng_init(seq=None)` derived the default curand subsequence from `threadIdx.x`
and `blockIdx.x` only. Every thread that differed only in `y`/`z` therefore
shared one subsequence, so e.g. the two threads at `(tx, 0)` and `(tx, 1)` of a
2-D block produced byte-identical draws.

Fold every launched dimension into the default sequence in row-major order.
Dimensions that were not launched have extent 1 and contribute nothing, so the
historical 1-D id `threadIdx.x + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x` is unchanged.

Fixes #2625

## Changes

`tilelang/cuda/language/random.py`
- add `_default_rng_sequence()`, a row-major linear id over every launched
  thread and block dimension;
- document the derived default in the `seq` parameter docstring.

`testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_rand.py`
- 4 new cases: 2-D thread block, 2-D grid, 1-D layout preservation, and an
  explicit `seq=` control.

## Validation

Environment: NVIDIA L20 (sm_89), CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128,
Python 3.13.14; base `e40e09e3e61595083d63a38bcf67f7ccb976b2ea` (current `main`).
`bash format.sh` passes on every changed file.

### Observable behaviour

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| generated sequence | `curand_init(1234, ((int)threadIdx.x), 0, &state)` | `curand_init(1234, ((((int)threadIdx.y) * 2) + ((int)threadIdx.x)), 0, &state)` |
| 4 threads of a 2x2 block | 2 distinct values, row collisions `[True, True]` | 4/4 distinct, `[False, False]` |
| 2x2 `blockIdx` grid | `blockIdx.y` ignored | `blockIdx.y` folded in |
| 1-D launch | — | byte-identical to explicit `seq = threadIdx.x + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x` |
| explicit `seq=` | forwarded | forwarded unchanged |

### Test results

`testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_rand.py`:

| build | result |
|---|---|
| before (unpatched `main`) | **2 failed, 8 passed** |
| after | **10 passed** |

The two failures before the patch are exactly the new regressions:

```text
FAILED test_rand_default_seq_covers_thread_y
FAILED test_rand_default_seq_covers_block_y
```

title: [BugFix][CUDA][RNG] Diagnose rng_rand/rng_rand_float without rng_init
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/3244/files) against `main`.

## Summary

A function that draws from the curand stream without ever calling `rng_init`
emitted `curand(&)`: the state name was empty, so a TileLang semantic error
surfaced as an nvcc syntax error inside generated code.

Validate RNG state once per function, in the existing `AddFunction` pre-scan. If
the body contains an `rng_rand` / `rng_rand_float` but no `rng_init`, fail with
an intentional TileLang error instead.

Fixes #3034

## Changes

`src/cuda/codegen/codegen_cuda.cc`
- extend the `AddFunction` pre-scan to record whether the function declares an
  `rng_init` and whether it consumes the stream, and check the combination. The
  check is deliberately **function-scoped rather than
  control-flow-sensitive**: an `rng_init` inside a runtime branch still counts
  as an initialisation, so this does not become definite-initialisation
  analysis.
- clear the per-function curand state name and type, so a draw cannot reference
  the state registered by an earlier function of the same module.

`testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_rand.py`
- 10 new cases: all five producer shapes without `rng_init`, plus the five
  positive controls.

## Validation

Python 3.13.14; base `e40e09e3e61595083d63a38bcf67f7ccb976b2ea` (current `main`).

| `rng_rand()` | nvcc syntax error, generated `curand(&)` | TileLang: ``requires a preceding `T.rng_init(...)` `` |
| `rng_rand_float()` | same | same intentional error |

title: [BugFix][CuTeDSL] Repair FP4 conversion/store lowering and packed FP4 output shapes
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/3241/files) against `main`.

## Summary

Repairs the CuTeDSL conversion/store path for sub-byte float types. With these changes the
**FP4** activation-quantization path compiles and passes under `target="cutedsl"`, and the FP8
destination-type mismatch is fixed as well.

The combined `test_example_act_quant` still fails, because its FP8 stage now reaches a
separate `libNVVM` compilation failure (see the verification section at the end and
#3240), so it cannot be removed from `CUTEDSL_KNOWN_FAILURES` yet.

Refs #3240
Related: #1454

## Changes

### 1. FP4 conversion helpers use the CUTLASS DSL 4.7 MLIR API

`tilelang/contrib/cutedsl/utils.py` converted between `float4_e2m1fn` and float vectors with
`vector.extractelement` / `vector.insertelement`. Those ops no longer exist in the `vector`
dialect shipped with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.7 (they are `vector.extract` / `vector.insert`
now), so every FP4 cast raised

```text
AttributeError: module 'cutlass._mlir.dialects.vector' has no attribute 'extractelement'
  at tilelang/contrib/cutedsl/utils.py:256 in _float32_to_f4e2m1_tensor
```

The helpers now use `vector.extract(v, [], [idx])` / `vector.insert(v, dst, [], [idx])`, which
also removes the now-unneeded dynamic index constants.

### 2. Sub-byte outputs are allocated packed

`CuTeDSLKernelAdapter._convert_torch_func` materialized outputs as
`torch.empty(*param_shapes[i], dtype=param_dtypes[i])` from the *logical* TIR shape. For a
4-bit dtype the torch storage type (`float4_e2m1fn_x2`) packs two elements per byte, so the
last dimension has to be divided by the packing factor — exactly what the CUDA adapters
already do (`stride_scale` in `tilelang/jit/adapter/tvm_ffi.py`). Without this,
`fp4_act_quant` returned `(M, N)` instead of the packed `(M, N/2)`:

```text
AssertionError: Shape mismatch: torch.Size([64, 256]) vs torch.Size([64, 128])
```

Measured A/B with the fix toggled (same script, same GPU):

| | returned shape |
|---|---|
| without this hunk | `(256,)` |
| with this hunk | `(128,)` |

### 3. The wrapper's FP8 dtype key matches the codegen

`TLCuTeDSLSourceWrapper._TYPE_MAP` mapped the TIR dtype string `"float8_e4m3"` to
`cutlass.Float8E4M3`, while `src/cuda/codegen/codegen_cutedsl.cc` only emits
`Float8E4M3FN` ("Only Float8E4M3FN is supported at the moment"). Since the TIR string for
`float8_e4m3fn` is `float8_e4m3`, generated fake tensors got `Float8E4M3` and every fp8
store attempted the unsupported conversion

```text
TypeError: Unsupported destination float type: Float8E4M3
  at cutlass/base_dsl/typing.py:1123 in Numeric.to
```

Both keys now map to `Float8E4M3FN`.

### 4. Focused regression test

`testing/python/jit/test_tilelang_jit_cutedsl_fp4_convert.py` covers the packed output shape
and decodes every stored nibble back to a representable FP4 E2M1 value, so the lowering is
not only exercised through the full DeepSeek example.

## Validation

NVIDIA L20 (sm_89), CUDA 12.8.61, PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0`, current
`main` at `e688a439a8f79d69497d02c4fad7c75fada954ad`.

Note that `TILELANG_TARGET=cutedsl` does not actually select this backend (only
`examples/conftest.py` reads it); the results below use `TILELANG_DEFAULT_TARGET=cutedsl` /
`target="cutedsl"`. That mismatch is reported in #3240.

| target | `test_fp8_act_quant` | `test_fp4_act_quant` | `test_round_trip_error` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cuda` before/after | pass | pass | pass |
| `cutedsl` before | `TypeError: Unsupported destination float type` | `AttributeError: ... extractelement` | same as FP8 |
| `cutedsl` after | libNVVM failure (unchanged, see below) | **pass** | libNVVM failure |

`test_fp4_act_quant` under CuTeDSL now reports `85/8192` packed bytes differing from the
PyTorch reference, all at FP4 rounding tie-breaks (max dequantized difference `0.5`), which
is the same behavior the CUDA backend documents.

```text
$ pytest -q testing/python/jit/test_tilelang_jit_cutedsl_fp4_convert.py
2 passed
```

## What this does not fix

The FP8 half of the same example still fails inside libNVVM
(`NVVM_ERROR_COMPILATION` on a minimal `bf16 -> float8_e4m3fn` elementwise store, with an
empty backend log), so `test_example_act_quant` remains in `CUTEDSL_KNOWN_FAILURES`. That
blocker, its minimal reproducer and the `TILELANG_TARGET` finding are tracked in #3240.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary

- Updated FP4 conversion lowering to use CUTLASS DSL 4.7 `vector.extract` and `vector.insert`.
- Packed sub-byte output shapes by dividing the final dimension by the packing factor.
- Mapped `float8_e4m3` and `float8_e4m3fn` to `cutlass.Float8E4M3FN`.
- Added regression tests for packed FP4 output and decoded FP4 values.

## Validation

- FP4 activation quantization passes in the reported environment.
- 85 of 8192 packed bytes differ only at rounding tie-breaks.
- FP8 validation remains blocked by a libNVVM compilation failure and is tracked in issue `#3240`.
- Review finding counts are unavailable from the supplied evidence.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


---

## Independent verification

Reproduced on `e40e09e3` (current `main`) with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0`, NVIDIA L20
(sm_89), CUDA 12.8. Backend selected with `TILELANG_DEFAULT_TARGET=cutedsl` — note that
`TILELANG_TARGET=cutedsl` does **not** select a backend (only `examples/conftest.py` reads
it, to attach xfails), so it cannot be used to check this PR.

`test_example_act_quant` was split into its three sub-paths, each run in isolation, with the
tilelang kernel cache cleared between arms (the cache key is the git commit, so the patched
and unpatched builds would otherwise share entries).

| sub-path | unpatched `main` | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_fp4_act_quant` | FAIL `module 'cutlass._mlir.dialects.vector' has no attribute 'extractelement'` | **PASS** |
| `test_fp8_act_quant` | FAIL `TypeError: Unsupported destination float type: Float8E4M3` | FAIL `CompilerDiagnosticError: NVVM backend compilation failed` |
| `test_round_trip_error` | FAIL (FP8) | FAIL (NVVM) |
| combined `test_example_act_quant` | FAIL | **FAIL** |
| this PR's focused regression `test_tilelang_jit_cutedsl_fp4_convert.py` | n/a | **PASS** (2 passed) |

So both code fixes in this PR are real and verified: the FP4 conversion helpers now use the
CUTLASS DSL 4.7 `vector.extract`/`vector.insert` API, and the `Float8E4M3` -> `Float8E4M3FN`
type-map fix removes the `Unsupported destination float type` error. What remains is the
`libNVVM` failure on the FP8 store path, which is a different problem already tracked in
#3240.

title: [TileIR] Add a CUDA Tile IR execution backend
body:
## Summary

Add a `tileir` execution backend that lowers TileLang programs to NVIDIA CUDA Tile IR and launches the assembled cubin through the cuTile runtime. This includes JIT compilation, caching, autotuning, typed IR lowering, and source-language semantic checks before TileIR launch materialization.

- Target CUDA Tile IR 13.4 bindings / tileiras 13.4 / cuTile 1.5, with installation documentation and a dedicated CI job that builds the pinned bindings.
- Keep TileIR launch and copy hints in `tilelang.tileir.language`, compatible with the current common language APIs.
- Include the tuned DeepSeek V4 sparse-attention kernel and its FP16/BF16 regression tests. Pro defaults use H128/BN64/CTA2; Flash H64/D512/topk512 uses H64/CTA1/eight worker warps. The example documents both configurations and the cuTile stride limit.
- Preserve attention sinks, masked padding, and zero output for all-padding queries. Stage and reuse TopK indices, with TMA disabled for the index copy.
- Cover packed tensor dispatch, loop-carried state, conditional load tokens, and explicit unsupported-example diagnostics.

## Validation

Validated on NVIDIA B200 with Python 3.12, CUDA Tile IR v13.4.0 bindings, tileiras 13.4.92, and cuTile 1.5.0. The native library was rebuilt using the compute node's CUDA 13.5 toolkit; generated CUDA kernels and TileIR used the 13.4.92 tools.

- Sparse-attention correctness: **14 passed**, including Pro/Flash schedules, FP16/BF16, padding, and all-padding rows.
- TileIR, TileIR JIT/cache/runtime/autotuning, atomic-save, backend registration, and constant-rebind regression coverage: **758 passed, 2 expected failures**.
- Eager frontend test file: **7 passed** after installing the missing CCCL headers in the test environment.
- Pro and Flash command-line examples passed sampled reference checks; measured **2.957 ms** and **0.119 ms**, respectively, with the documented B200 configurations.
- `bash format.sh`, `git diff --check`, and Python 3.10 syntax checks for all 128 changed Python files passed.

title: [BugFix][CMake] Keep an SDK path given through the backend environment variables
body:
## Summary

`USE_CUDA`, `USE_ROCM`, `USE_METAL` and `USE_LLVM` are documented to take a path as well as a boolean — `TILELANG_BACKEND_DOC_CUDA` reads `Enable CUDA backend (ON/OFF/or CUDA SDK path)` — and a path works when it arrives through `-DUSE_CUDA=<path>`. Through the environment it does not: the value is coerced to `ON` or `OFF` by `if($ENV{USE_CUDA})`, and `if()` treats a string that is not a boolean constant as a variable name. `/opt/cuda` names no variable, so the test is false and the backend is turned off.

Nothing reports this. The configure step succeeds, the build succeeds, and the library it installs has no object from `src/cuda` in it. The first sign is at run time, far from the cause: `AttributeError: module 'tilelang.cuda._ffi_api' has no attribute 'AnnotateDeviceBoundTmaCopies'`.

The value now reaches the cache variable as written, which is what `-D` already does. Booleans are unaffected, because the variable is read back with `if(USE_CUDA)` and a defined variable is tested against its value rather than re-read as a name:

| `USE_CUDA=` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | ON | true, value `1` |
| `ON` | ON | true, value `ON` |
| `OFF` | OFF | false, value `OFF` |
| `0` | OFF | false, value `0` |
| `/opt/cuda` | **OFF** | **true, value `/opt/cuda`** |

The four backends carried four copies of the same block, so the fix is one loop over the `TILELANG_BACKENDS` list the file already defines and already loops over three times above.

## Validation

The table above is `cmake -P` on CMake 4.4.3, each row a separate `set(ENV{...})`.

A/B on one GH200 (sm_90, aarch64), CUDA 13.1, configure only, same tree at `6679f913` and the same `USE_CUDA=<sdk path>` in the environment, the patch the only difference:

| | `CUDA Backend is enabled` | configure stops at |
|---|---|---|
| before | absent | `FindZ3`, on the no-CUDA path |
| after | **present** | `Could NOT find CUDAToolkit (missing: CUDA_CUDART)`, inside `src/cuda` |

The run after the patch still stops, one stage later and for a different reason: on aarch64 `find_package(CUDAToolkit)` looks for the runtime under `targets/<arch>/lib`, which a toolkit laid out with `include` and `lib64` at its root does not have. That is a separate problem and not what this changes; the discriminator here is whether the CUDA backend is entered at all.

Reading `USE_CUDA` back out of `CMakeCache.txt` does not show the difference — it says `OFF` either way. The assignment is a directory-scope variable that shadows the cache entry, so the cache keeps the `option()` default. The message is the signal.

- Updated CMake backend selection for `CUDA`, `ROCM`, `METAL`, and `LLVM`.

- Replaced duplicated backend-specific logic with a loop over `TILELANG_BACKENDS`.
- Added validation for boolean values, path values, and CUDA configuration with an environment-provided SDK path.

title: [BugFix][JIT] Allocate a dynamic-shape output that precedes its sizing input
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3017.

A `@tilelang.jit` kernel whose **output** has a symbolic dimension and appears *before* the input that supplies that dimension crashed at call time with `IndexError: list index out of range`. The kernel compiled fine; the crash was in the host wrapper that allocates the output.

Two things had to line up, and both are fixed:

**1. The symbolic dimension was owned by the output itself.** `_process_dynamic_symbolic` walked the parameters in signature order and recorded each symbolic dimension against the first parameter whose buffer mentioned it, without excluding outputs. For `main(B(N,), A(N,))` with `out_idx=[0]` the entry came out as `N: (0, 0, 0, 1)` — owner index `0` is `B`, the output being allocated. Inputs are now visited first, so the entry is `N: (0, 1, 0, 1)` — the input `A`.

**2. The caller built its tensor list in a single pass.** Even with the owner pointing at an input, an output at parameter 0 would still have read `tensor_list[1]` before it was filled. Both adapters now place all input tensors first and allocate the outputs afterwards, in parameter order.

`tilelang/jit/adapter/tvm_ffi.py` and `tilelang/jit/adapter/cython/{adapter.py,cython_wrapper.pyx}` get the same two changes; they are duplicated implementations of the same logic.

## Test plan

Added `test_cython_dynamic_shape_output_before_input` to `testing/python/jit/test_tilelang_jit_cython.py`.

Hardware: NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB (sm80), CUDA 12.8, tilelang built from source at `66c003c` (the `.pyx` change has to be compiled, so the pip wheel cannot exercise it).

A/B on the same tree, stashing only `tilelang/jit/adapter/` and rebuilding in between:

| backend | shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cython` | output last (control) | OK, map `N: (0, 0, 0, 1)` | OK, map unchanged |
| `cython` | **output first** | **`IndexError`** at `cython_wrapper.pyx:202` | **OK**, results match, map `N: (0, 1, 0, 1)` |
| `tvm_ffi` | output first | OK — see note | OK |

The new test is `1 failed` before and `1 passed` after. `testing/python/jit/test_tilelang_jit_cython.py` is `1 passed, 1 skipped` after (the skip is the PDL test, which requires sm90). `testing/python/profiler/test_tilelang_profiler_dynamic_symbolic.py` is `11 passed`.

Two things worth being explicit about:

- **The `tvm_ffi` adapter's preallocated-output path is not the default on current main.** It is only taken when the host target is not the C host, because the callee-allocated-output ABI otherwise short-circuits `_convert_torch_func` entirely. I fixed it because the defect is identical and the code is a duplicate, but the test above covers the `cython` backend, which is where the bug is reachable today. I exercised the `tvm_ffi` path separately by forcing `_uses_ffi_callee_allocated_output_abi()` to return `False`: before the fix it raises the same `IndexError` with `N: (0, 0, 0, 1)`, after the fix it completes with `N: (0, 1, 0, 1)`. Note that forcing only the Python side leaves the lowered function on the callee-allocated ABI, so the numerical result in that setup is meaningless for both sides of that comparison — it is the disappearance of the `IndexError` and the owner change that it demonstrates.
- **Renamed API.** The reproducer in the issue uses `T.symbolic`, which current main renamed to `T.dynamic` (`tilelang/language/symbolics.py`, `__all__ = ["dynamic"]`). I reproduced and tested against `T.dynamic`; the defect is unchanged.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on the changed Python files, and `clang-format` reports no changes on the `.pyx`.

## Adjacent observation (not changed here)

In the same resolution loop, the scalar-parameter case (`ref_id == 2`) indexes the caller's argument list with the *parameter* index:

```python
if ref_id == 2:
    shape.append(inputs[ref_tensor_idx])
```

That is only correct while no output precedes the scalar parameter. It looks wrong for the same reason the reported bug was, but I have no reproduction for it and did not want to change behaviour I cannot demonstrate, so I left it alone and mention it rather than guess.

title: [BugFix][CUDA] Lower a kernel-body assert to a device-legal check
[Bugfix] Carry memory_order through vectorized atomic_add
body:
Fixes #2688.

## Cause

`vectorize_loop.cc` rebuilt the wide atomic from two operands:

```cpp
return Call(op->dtype, GetVectorizedAtomicOp(vector_size), {dst, src});
```

The region lowering puts `memory_order` in `args[2]`. Codegen appends it only under
`if (op->args.size() > 2)`, so the emitted `AtomicAddx2(dst, src)` picks up the
`= memory_order_relaxed` default on the device function. Legal C++, no diagnostic anywhere.
Everything downstream already accepted the operand, including `num_inputs = 3`; the vectorizer
was under-filling it.

The fix carries the trailing operands through, starting at index 2 because the two-argument form
is legal, and copying rather than visiting because the order is lane-invariant.

## Why atomic.h changes too

Carrying the order makes inline PTX reachable that had never been assembled: the non-relaxed
branches were constant-folded away while the order always defaulted to relaxed. Three of them do
not build.

1. **fp16 used `.v2.f16`**, whose vector operands require sm_90, and fp16 vectorizes to x2 on
   every target. Now uses packed `f16x2`, available from sm_60 and emitting identical SASS on
   sm_90, so fp16 needs no arch guard at all and the per-half pack/unpack goes away.
2. **bf16 was missing `.noftz`**, which ptxas requires for `.bf16`. Syntax error on every target,
   sm_90 included.
3. **bf16 has no ordered atomic below sm_90 at any width**, so unlike fp16 there is nothing to
   fall back to. The sm_90 path is guarded, with `__threadfence()` around a relaxed bf16x2
   atomicAdd below it: two-way where release and acquire need one-way, so conservative rather
   than lossy.

New guards use `__CUDA_ARCH__` rather than the `__CUDA_ARCH_LIST__` spelling elsewhere in this
file, which fails a `-gencode` multi-arch build with `C1012`. The remaining uses guard
declarations, where `__CUDA_ARCH__` is undefined in the host pass, so those stay as they are.

Docstrings for `atomic_add`, `atomic_max` and `atomic_min` claimed the region path ignores
`memory_order`, which is no longer true.

## Testing

Six cases covering acquire, release and acq_rel on fp16 and bf16, since each ordering is a
separately spelled asm string. Each asserts on the generated CUDA, then runs the kernel.

RTX 2000 Ada (sm_89), CUDA 13.3: **56 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed**. The failure is
`test_tma_atomic_add`, which fails identically on unmodified `main` (TMA needs sm_90 and that
test has no arch guard) and uses no `memory_order`.

Negative control: reverting only the two source files, keeping the new tests, and rebuilding
makes them fail with `AtomicAddx2((&(Out[...])), *(uint1*)(X + ...));`. Restoring and rebuilding
makes them pass.

Every PTX spelling was checked against sm_75 through sm_90 with ptxas. There is no sm_90
hardware here, so those branches are verified to assemble rather than to run.

## One untested path

`AtomicAddx2Ret(bfloat16_t*)` takes the same guard through the shared helper, and
`AtomicAddx4Ret` routes through it. This is the only part with no test, and it cannot have one:
nothing reachable instantiates the bf16 Ret overloads with a non-relaxed order, since
`GetVectorizedAtomicOp` returns only the non-ret ops, `T.atomic_addx2` / `T.atomic_addx4` take no
`memory_order`, and region-form `return_prev=True` raises `NotImplementedError`. Guarded anyway
so the file stays consistent and the path is already correct when `return_prev` is implemented.
Verified by instantiating the template directly: without the guard it fails on sm_80/86/89 with
`Instruction 'atom.add.bf16.global' requires .target sm_90 or higher`, and passes on all four
targets with it.

title: [BugFix] Reject non-power-of-two AllReduce thread strides
body:
## Summary

`tl::AllReduce` is an XOR butterfly: thread `t` pairs with `t ^ (scale * k)`. That only moves the reduce coordinate when `scale` (the thread stride between consecutive reduce participants) is a power of two. #2611 added the power-of-two check for the logical width (`threads / scale`) but not for the stride itself, so a stride-3 reduce slipped through the lowering, the CUDA `static_assert`, and the reducer v2 planner.

The natural trigger is any fragment whose non-reduced extent is not a power of two: reducing a `(32, 3)` fragment along `dim=0` with its default inferred layout (`thread = i * 3 + j + 96 * rep`) lowers to `AllReduce<MaxOp, 96, 3>`. Depending on the CTA size this either silently mixes columns and replicas (256 threads: `reduce_max` of `arange(96).reshape(32, 3)` returns `[63, 62, 62]` instead of `[93, 94, 95]`) or reads past the workspace (`t ^ 48` for `t >= 64` with exactly 96 or 192 threads: `illegal memory access`). The same shape shows up in an FP4 → FP8 scaling-factor cast kernel whenever `hidden / out_block_k` is not a power of two.

## Changes

- `CheckAllReduceWidth` (shared by `tl.reduce` and `tl.finalize_reducer`) now also requires `scale` to be a power of two, with an error that points at padding the non-reduced fragment extent.
- `tl::AllReduce` in the CUDA template carries the matching `static_assert`.
- The reducer v2 narrow-plan gate (`AnalyzeReducerUpdateSite`) rejects non-power-of-two strides alongside the existing width check, so the planner falls back to the wide plan instead of emitting the broken collective (`(32, 3) -> (3,)` max over 128 threads now produces a correct `AllReduce<MaxOp, 128, 1>`).

Non-power-of-two strides are deliberately rejected rather than supported: such layouts are already slower than their power-of-two-padded counterparts, so the right fix on the kernel side is to pad.

## Tests

- `test_allreduce_rejects_non_power_of_two_scale` (reduce, sum/max × three trigger shapes: exact-fit 96 threads, two replicas over 256 threads, shuffle-only width).
- `test_narrow_plan_rejects_non_power_of_two_thread_stride` (reducer v2: asserts the wide fallback plan and checks the result).

## Validation

- `testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_reduce.py`, `test_tilelang_language_reducer_v2.py`, `testing/python/transform/test_tilelang_transform_reducer_scalar_candidates.py`: 189 passed. The 3 remaining failures (`test_reduce[sum-float16-64x128-f2f-t256-b4]`, `[sum-bfloat16-64x128-f2f-t256-b4]`, `[min-float16-128x128-f2f-t256-b8]`, `batch <= N_total`) are pre-existing on this sm_100-class machine and unrelated to this change.
- `format.sh` clean.

Add SM120 dense block-scaled MMA and essential support for SageAttention3
body:
## Summary

This PR adds SM120 block-scale MMA support and the TileLang compiler/runtime features needed to implement SageAttention3 FP4 raw-core kernels in pure TileLang. It introduces a generic `T.ptx_mma_blockscale` intrinsic for `mxf8f6f4` and `mxf4nvf4`, adds the SM120 SageAttention3 FP4 example kernel, and fixes reduce/storage-sync lowering needed by the new path and existing language tests.

## Changes

- Add `tl.ptx_mma_blockscale` builtin and Python frontend bindings.
- Add CUDA codegen support for lowering block-scale MMA calls through `tl::mma_sync_blockscale`.
- Add `mma_blockscale.h` with SM120 block-scale MMA dispatcher specializations.
- Add PTX-side validation metadata for supported block-scale MMA configs:
  - `mxf8f6f4`, `m16n8k32`, `scale_vec=1`, `ue8m0`
  - `mxf4nvf4`, `m16n8k64`, `scale_vec=2`, `ue8m0`
  - `mxf4nvf4`, `m16n8k64`, `scale_vec=4`, `ue4m3`
- Add `PrintMMABlockScaleAssembly` helpers and shared dtype/string mapping for block-scale MMA validation.

- Add `T.pack_b16` for packing four b16 values into a global store.
- Add `examples/sage_attention_sm120` with a pure TileLang SM120 SageAttention3 FP4 raw-core kernel and helper macros.
- Extend `T.ptx_ldmatrix` with optional matrix shape/dtype metadata and add CUDA lowering for `m8n16.x4.shared.b8x16.b4x16_p64`.
- Add `T.lds32` and CUDA shared-memory 32-bit load helpers for packed scale/FP4 data paths.
- Add strict `T.copy(..., prefer_instruction="ldsm"|"stsm")` handling so matrix-copy requests fail clearly instead of silently falling back.
- Add `T.tma_copy(..., tma_element_dtype=...)` and improve TMA descriptor projection, folded base offsets, `elem_offset` handling, and transaction-byte accounting.
- Preserve explicit pack lanes when reshaping packed byte/sub-byte layouts.
- Add `role_scoped=True` allocation support so branch-local register arrays can stay inside warp-specialized producer/consumer roles.
- Improve CUDA codegen for scoped `pragma_unroll_factor`, aligned narrow local allocations, and FP4 local `address_of`.

- Update `ReduceLowerer` batch handling to clamp requested batch size to the physical per-thread output element count before divisibility checks.
- Use float32 temporary accumulators for fp16/bf16 `sum` and `abssum`, then cast back to the destination dtype.
- Avoid packed fp16/bf16 sum reducers where low-precision pairwise accumulation can exceed existing reduce-test tolerances.
- Remove allocation-wide alias ranges from thread-storage-sync disjointness proofs so pointer/buffer conflict checks stay conservative.

- Add handle byte offset support in TMA descriptor parsing for nvrtc

title: [Metal] Support 32-bit integer atomic add
body:
## Problem

Metal cannot lower scalar signed or unsigned 32-bit `T.atomic_add` operations, including the form that returns the previous value. Portable kernels requiring integer counters or slot allocation therefore fail during Metal code generation.

## Change

- Lower scalar `int32` and `uint32` atomic-add calls to Metal `atomic_fetch_add_explicit`.

title: [ROCm] Add safe-gated KDA decode example
body:
## Summary

- add a TileLang packed decode kernel for safe-gated KDA
- update a slot-indexed recurrent state pool in place and return the decode output
- add ROCm correctness coverage for output/state parity, multiple steps, dummy state indices, reordered slots, configurable bounds, and the GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 local shape
- document the packed decode contract under `examples/kda`

## Kernel contract

The kernel consumes post-convolution packed QKV plus raw gate inputs `a` and `b`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`, an FP32 state pool, and per-request state indices. It computes:

```text
g = lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (a + dt_bias))
beta = sigmoid(b)
```

It applies Q/K L2 normalization, performs the delta-rule recurrent update, mutates the selected state slots, and writes `[batch, 1, value_heads, value_dim]` output. Negative state indices produce zero output and do not access or mutate the state pool.

The implementation is parameterized by dimensions and does not contain model-name or GPU-architecture dispatch. The documented GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 specialization is eight local Q/K/V heads with `key_dim=value_dim=128` and `lower_bound=-5.0`.

title: [Bugfix][Subtype] Fix scalar fp4 store/load codegen for non-packed buffers
body:
## Problem

Two issues with `float4_e2m1fn` (`fp4`) when `T.StridedTensor` uses **dynamic** strides (`T.dynamic()`):

### 1. Frontend stride capture is wrong for dynamic strides

fp4 packs 2 elements per byte, so the logical element stride is **2x the byte stride** reported by PyTorch's DLTensor. When strides are dynamic (runtime-resolved), the Python adapters (`tvm_ffi.py`, `cython/adapter.py`) read the runtime stride but did not apply this scaling factor, passing incorrect (halved) strides to the kernel.

(When strides are static/compile-time constants, `MakePackedAPI` in `arg_binder.cc` already handles the `* pack_factor` scaling correctly — so this only affects dynamic strides.)

### 2. Codegen scalar fp4 store corrupts neighboring nibbles

When strides are dynamic, the compiler cannot vectorize the store and falls back to element-by-element writes. `GetBufferRef` in `codegen_cuda.cc` applies a `/2` index mapping for fp4 (since 2 elements share 1 byte), but the scalar write stores a full byte (`fp4_e2_t` = `uint8_t`), destroying the neighboring nibble:

```c
// i=0: cache_fp4[0] = 0x0L   ← low nibble written, high nibble zeroed
// i=1: cache_fp4[0] = 0x0H   ← overwrites! low nibble from i=0 is lost
```

The same kernel with static (compile-time constant) strides takes the vectorized path `*(fp4_e2_32_t*)ptr = ...` and produces correct results.

## Minimal reproduction

```python
@tilelang.jit(out_idx=None, target="cuda")
def dynamic_kern(block_size: int) -> object:
    ds0 = T.dynamic("ds0")
    ds1 = T.dynamic("ds1")

    @T.prim_func
    def f(src: T.Tensor((n, 128), T.float4_e2m1fn),
          dst: T.StridedTensor((num_blocks, block_size, 128),
                               (ds0, ds1, 1), T.float4_e2m1fn), ...) -> None:
        with T.Kernel(n, threads=32) as i:
            for k in T.serial(128):
                dst[slots[i] // block_size,
                    slots[i] % block_size, k] = src[i, k]
    return f
```

## Changes

* **codegen_cuda.cc**: Scalar fp4 load/store to non-packed buffers now uses `tl_fp4_packed_load` / `tl_fp4_packed_store` for nibble-safe read-modify-write
* **cython/adapter.py, cython_wrapper.pyx, tvm_ffi.py**: Add `stride_scale = 8 // element_bits` to `_process_dynamic_symbolic` so dynamic strides for sub-byte dtypes are correctly scaled from byte units to logical element units
* **inject_assumes.cc**: Extend `InjectAssumes` pass to emit `assume(stride % pack_factor == 0)` for non-last-dimension strides of sub-byte buffers, providing the TIR analyzer with divisibility information
* **test_tilelang_language_subtype.py**: Add two tests:
  - `test_subtype_fp4_dynamic_stride_store`: compares static vs dynamic stride fp4 scatter byte-for-byte
  - `test_subtype_fp4_scalar_store_codegen`: scatter via indirection forces scalar store path, verifies nibble correctness

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_subtype.py` → 34/34 passed

title: Refactor ptx_ldmatrix to use tl.access_ptr with simplified signature
body:
## Summary

- Replace the legacy 8-parameter TVM-style `ptx_ldmatrix` API with a 4-parameter TileLang-style API that uses `tl.access_ptr` wrapping `BufferLoad`

## Details

The new `ptx_ldmatrix` signature is:

```
ptx_ldmatrix(trans, num, src_access_ptr, dst_access_ptr)
```

Where both `src_access_ptr` and `dst_access_ptr` are `T.access_ptr(buf[indices], rw_mask, extent)` calls. This preserves buffer metadata (BufferLoad + extent + rw_mask) for downstream analysis passes, unlike the old approach which used pre-computed byte offsets via `tvm_access_ptr`.

When tilelang is installed from a PyPI wheel, `LOG(WARNING)` messages currently leak the build machine's absolute file paths (e.g. `/home/runner/work/tilelang/tilelang/src/op/copy.cc:520`) because `__FILE__` is baked in at compile time. This is a poor user experience and exposes CI infrastructure details.

This PR enables TVM's `TVM_LOG_CUSTOMIZE` hook to take control of log output formatting, and conditionally strips source paths in release builds.

## Changes

- **Enable `TVM_LOG_CUSTOMIZE`** and provide custom `LogMessageImpl` / `LogFatalImpl` in `src/runtime/logging.cc`
- **Auto-detect release builds** via `CIBUILDWHEEL` and `SKBUILD_STATE` environment variables, exposed as the CMake option `TILELANG_RELEASE_BUILD`
- **Downgrade noisy diagnostics** from `LOG(WARNING)` to `DLOG(WARNING)` in `atomic_add.cc` and `producer_consumer_ws.cc` (these are development diagnostics, not actionable for end users)

### Behavior

| Build | `TILELANG_RELEASE_BUILD` | LOG(WARNING) output |
|---|---|---|
| Local dev (`pip install -e .`, `cmake .. && make`) | OFF | `[HH:MM:SS] /path/to/file.cc:123: Warning: msg` |
| Wheel (`cibuildwheel`, `python -m build`) | ON | `[HH:MM:SS] Warning: msg` |

No 3rdparty files are modified — the custom logging implementation lives entirely in tilelang-owned source.

## Test plan

- [x] Local build compiles and links successfully (`cmake --build . --target tilelang`)
- [x] `./format.sh` (pre-commit hooks) passes
- [ ] CI wheel build smoke test (`python -c "import tilelang; print(tilelang.__version__)"`)

title: [codex] Fix 1D TMA store layout inference
body:
This fixes a layout-inference regression that caused plain shared -> global copies to fall back from the pointer-based 1D TMA store path to descriptor-based multidimensional TMA.

Root cause: `CopyNode::InferLayout()` could still attach a swizzled shared-memory layout during free inference after the copy had already been selected as `kBulkStore1D`. That mutated the shared layout map and made later lowering reject the 1D path, which produced `CUtensorMap`-backed stores instead of `tl::tma_store(shared_ptr, global_ptr, bytes)`.

What changed:
- Skip shared-layout swizzle inference for copies that have already been classified as 1D TMA.
- Add a regression test that compiles a full-shape `(128, 128)` shared -> global store and checks that the generated kernel uses pointer-based `tma_store` without `CUtensorMap`.

Validation:
- `./format.sh`
- `cmake --build build -j$(nproc)`
- `python debug/0503_tma_store/test.py`
- `python -m pytest testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_tma_store.py -x -k "full_shape_tma_store_uses_1d"`

title: [BugFix] Fallback non-16B cluster bulk copies
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2506.

This PR prevents `T.copy_cluster` from emitting an invalid `cp.async.bulk` operation when the transfer size is not a multiple of 16 bytes.

For transfers that satisfy the bulk-copy requirements, the existing TMA-based cluster-copy path is preserved. For transfers whose byte size is not divisible by 16, the compiler now emits a warning and falls back to the regular cluster-copy implementation instead of generating a `tma_store_cluster` call with an ISA-invalid transfer size.

## Problem

The TMA lowering path for `T.copy_cluster` computes the transfer size from the number of elements and the element data type:

```text
size_bytes = number_of_elements * bytes_per_element
```

The resulting byte count was passed directly to `tma_store_cluster` without checking whether it was a multiple of 16.

For example, a copy of 127 `float32` elements has a transfer size of:

```text
127 * 4 = 508 bytes
```

The generated code could therefore contain a call equivalent to:

```cpp
tl::tma_store_cluster(..., static_cast<uint32_t>(508), ...);
```

The underlying `cp.async.bulk` instruction requires the transfer size to be a multiple of 16 bytes. Emitting a non-conforming size results in PTX-undefined behavior. Depending on the GPU and driver, this may manifest as a kernel hang, an unspecified launch failure, incorrect output, or another device-side failure.

This path does not use a tensor-map descriptor, so descriptor validation does not catch the invalid transfer size before it reaches the generated device code.

## Solution

This PR adds an eligibility check before selecting the TMA cluster-copy path.

The updated behavior is:

* If the transfer size is a multiple of 16 bytes, preserve the existing `tma_store_cluster` lowering.
* If the transfer size is not a multiple of 16 bytes:

  * emit a compiler warning explaining that the bulk-copy requirement is not satisfied;
  * skip the TMA lowering;
  * fall back to the regular element-wise cluster-copy path.

This keeps `T.copy_cluster` correct for arbitrary supported shapes while retaining the optimized TMA path for eligible transfers.

The fallback is intentionally not silent because it may have a meaningful performance impact. The warning makes the lowering decision visible without rejecting an otherwise valid high-level cluster-copy operation.

## Warning behavior

When the TMA path is skipped, the compiler emits a warning indicating that:

* `cp.async.bulk` requires a transfer size divisible by 16 bytes;
* the current transfer size does not satisfy that requirement;
* the operation is being lowered to the regular cluster-copy implementation.

Aligned copies do not emit this warning.

## Testcase correction

The original reproducer in #2506 also contained an independent cluster-programming issue.

It allowed every CTA in the cluster to execute:

```python
T.copy_cluster(..., dst_block=1, ...)
T.mbarrier_wait_parity(...)
```

With a two-CTA cluster, this means that both CTA 0 and CTA 1 issue a copy targeting cluster rank 1, and both CTAs wait on their local barrier. This mixes the transfer-size issue with producer/consumer role and barrier-synchronization behavior. In particular, an aligned transfer may still fail for reasons unrelated to the 16-byte bulk-copy requirement.

The regression test therefore assigns explicit CTA roles:

* CTA 0 initializes the source data and issues the remote cluster copy.
* CTA 1 waits on its local completion barrier and validates the received data.

The test also uses the current `T.ClusterKernel` API rather than passing `cluster_dims` to `T.Kernel`.

This isolates the lowering behavior under test and ensures that the only relevant difference between the aligned and non-aligned cases is TMA eligibility.

## Test coverage

The regression test covers both optimized and fallback behavior:

* An aligned `float32` transfer, such as 128 elements / 512 bytes:

  * still emits `tma_store_cluster`;
  * does not use the fallback;
  * completes successfully and produces the expected output.

* A non-aligned `float32` transfer, such as 127 elements / 508 bytes:

  * does not emit an invalid `tma_store_cluster`;
  * emits the fallback warning;
  * uses the regular cluster-copy path;
  * completes successfully and produces the expected output.

Additional boundary cases can cover aligned and non-aligned sizes on both sides of the boundary, such as 124 elements / 496 bytes and 126 elements / 504 bytes.

Tests are skipped on devices that do not support thread-block clusters.

## Behavioral impact

For valid TMA transfers, this change does not alter the generated bulk-copy path.

For non-16-byte-sized transfers, behavior changes from emitting an ISA-invalid bulk-copy operation to issuing a warning and using a correct, potentially slower fallback.

This prioritizes correctness while preserving the optimized implementation whenever its hardware requirements are satisfied.

## Scope

This PR addresses the transfer-size requirement for the cluster bulk-copy path. It does not synthesize shared-memory padding or otherwise enlarge source or destination allocations.

## Summary

- Fixes `T.copy_cluster` to prevent emitting ISA-undefined `cp.async.bulk`/bulk-copy lowering when the transfer byte size is not provably divisible by 16.
- Preserves the optimized TMA fast path (`tl::tma_store_cluster`) only when the transfer size is provably 16-byte aligned; otherwise it falls back to the regular SIMT/element-wise cluster-copy lowering.
- Adds compile-time validation for `tma_store_cluster` arguments in CUDA codegen by stripping `CastNode` wrappers before checking constants, and issues a compiler warning when the 16B-multiple requirement cannot be satisfied.
- Updates TMA row construction and barrier/row logic to safely propagate “cannot prove 16B multiple” failures via an `std::optional` return, guarding TMA-row/barrier emission so fallback paths remain correct.
- Adds regression tests covering:
  - non-16B contiguous and non-16B row-sized cluster copies (asserting `tl::tma_store_cluster` is not generated and `map_shared_rank`/SIMT fallback is used),

title: [Refactor][BugFix] Refactor the loop vectorization plan with ConstraintKind
body:
## Summary

- classify vectorization constraints explicitly as must-scalarize, call, cast, local, memory, or broadcast-load
- keep non-local invariant loads as scalar broadcasts without reusing the local/fragment category
- force ordinary loop-invariant stores to scalarize across global, shared, local, and fragment scopes while preserving the all-rep reducer exception
- add deterministic global and local accumulation regressions

## Motivation

`ComputeBufferVectorSize` already identifies ordinary invariant stores as requiring `vector_size=1`, but the old scope-based bucketing could discard that semantic requirement. The narrow fix in #2922 keeps global/shared stores in the memory bucket, while local/fragment stores can still lose the same constraint.

This change separates classification, aggregation, and strategy selection. `Plan()` now orchestrates those phases, broadcast loads have their own category, and a must-scalarize constraint returns width 1 before any memory/local strategy is selected.

Related: #2922

## ConstraintKind

| ConstraintKind | Classification condition | Typical example | Effect on vector size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kMustScalarize` | `requires_scalarization=true`; an ordinary invariant/independent store, excluding all-rep reducers | `acc[0] += A[i]`, `B[row] += A[row, i]` | Takes precedence over every strategy and selects `vector_size=1` |
| `kCall` | Not associated with a concrete buffer and not produced by a cast | A regular `CallNode` or condition expression | Contributes to both `call_min` and `non_cast_call_min` |
| `kCast` | Not associated with a concrete buffer and produced by a `CastNode` | A conversion from `float32` to `float16` | Contributes to `call_min`; may be deferred by `DecoupleTypeCast` in the simple memory strategy |
| `kLocal` | Buffer scope is `local`, `local.var`, or fragment | `local[i] = value`, fragment load/store | Contributes to `local_min`; deferred and revalidated under the simple memory strategy |
| `kMemory` | A non-local buffer access that is neither a broadcast load nor a must-scalarize store | `B[row, i] = A[row, i]`, regular global/shared load/store | Contributes to `memory_min` and enables the memory vectorization strategy |
| `kBroadcastLoad` | A non-local load whose address is invariant within the candidate vector boundary | Reading `C[row]` inside a vectorized loop | Treated as scalar load + broadcast; excluded from `memory_min` and revalidated if necessary |

## Testing

- `bash format.sh --files src/transform/loop_vectorize.cc testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_vectorize.py`
- `cmake --build build -j 32`
- `python -m pytest -q testing/python/language/test_tilelang_language_vectorize.py` — 36 passed
- `python -m pytest -q testing/python/transform/test_tilelang_transform_legalize_vectorized_loop.py::test_vectorize_access` — passed

title: [Bugfix][Transform] Make shared-memory offset assignment deterministic
body:
## Symptom

Compiling the **same kernel** twice can produce different (semantically equivalent) CUDA: which merged-arena slot each shared buffer gets — most visibly which AllReduce `workspace` alias each reduction uses — flips between runs. A reducer-heavy kernel compiled 5 times produced **5 distinct device sources**. Running under `setarch -R` (ASLR disabled) made all runs identical, pinning the cause on heap-pointer-ordered iteration: `std::hash<const void*>` is the pointer value, so any `unordered_map` keyed by node addresses iterates in an order that changes with heap layout.

This is harmless for correctness (liveness constraints hold under any processing order; only the pairing of buffers to equivalent slots permutes), but it breaks reproducible builds and any byte-identical-codegen validation methodology, and it makes diffing generated code across compiles useless.

## Root causes (both in `MergeSharedMemoryAllocations`)

1. **Kill-point reordering iterated the pointer-keyed `event_map_`** (`unordered_map<const Object*, EventEntry>`). The traversal order decides the order in which moved kill points are appended to their target statements, which decides the order freed slots re-enter the free list, which decides which slot the next allocation grabs. Fixed by walking the deterministic linearized statement sequence instead.

2. **Every sort in the planner tie-broke by `name_hint`, which is not unique.** Every AllReduce scratch buffer is literally named `workspace` (one test kernel has 11 of them), and double-buffered stages share their buffer's name. Fully-tied groups (same liveness start, same size, same name) fell back to `std::sort`'s unspecified order on unordered_map-derived input. Fixed by recording each allocation's IR-visit discovery index in `AllocateCollector` and using it as the final tie-break in `PlanMemory`, `LinearScanPack`, `MakeAliasBindings`, and `PlanSequentialLayout` — every comparator is now a total order.

## ODR landmine found along the way

`lower_thread_allreduce.cc` defines a *different* `tvm::tl::AllocateCollector`. Both classes had external linkage, so the linker deduplicated their vague-linkage inline members across translation units — an ODR violation that stayed silently benign only while the two layouts happened to match, and corrupted the collector (garbage `unordered_map` state → `std::bad_alloc`) the moment this patch added a field to one of them. The collector here now lives in an anonymous namespace.

## Validation

- The 5-distinct-hashes reproducer now yields **1 identical hash across 8 runs** with ASLR enabled; two other previously-flipping kernels are likewise stable (3/3 identical each).
- Language suite: 1172 passed, 137 skipped. reducer_v2 suite: 75 passed. All 17 downstream reducer-heavy production kernels compile and pass numerics.

Discovered while validating tile-ai/tvm#68 (byte-identical codegen check kept flipping); independent of that PR.

title: [Compiler][Z3] Bump 3rdparty/tvm to materialize Z3 solvers lazily
body:
## Motivation

`arith::Analyzer` carries a `Z3Prover` whose implementation eagerly creates a `z3::solver` at construction and translates every `Bind`/`EnterConstraint` into z3 constraints up front. Analyzers are scratch objects created in huge numbers during lowering — `InverseWithLevel`, `OutputShape`, per-op inference analyzers, etc. — so a single reducer-heavy kernel compile creates **~67k Z3 solvers** and issues **~100k z3 asserts**, while instrumentation shows only **~0.3% of analyzers ever reach the Z3 fallback** of `CanProve`. Profiling attributes 40%+ of such compiles to Z3 solver init and bind translation.

This became prominent after #3093: PartialFragment layouts disabled the fully-replicated shortcut in `ProveFragmentContains`, roughly doubling the number of analyzer-heavy containment proofs during layout inference, which regressed reducer-heavy kernel compiles by up to ~2x.

## What this bumps

tile-ai/tvm#68 — Z3 solvers are now materialized lazily: binds and constraints are journaled (reusing the existing `scope_stack_` bookkeeping), and the first operation that actually needs the solver creates it and replays the journal in order. Semantics are preserved exactly; see the tvm PR for the full design and edge cases (assume-mode side effects, `CopyFrom`, replay ordering).

## Results

On a suite of 17 downstream reducer-heavy production kernels (H100, cold compiles, kernel cache disabled), the worst #3093 regressors improve 40-60% end-to-end and land **below their pre-#3093 compile times**:

| kernel (end-to-end, incl. ~6.6s fixed test overhead) | pre-#3093 | #3093 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| reducer kernel #1 | 15.3s | 23.7s | **12.9s** |
| reducer kernel #2 | 15.2s | 18.8s | **11.2s** |
| reducer kernel #3 | 11.1s | 14.3s | **10.5s** |

`tilelang.lower` roughly halves across the board, including non-reducer kernels (toy GEMM 0.23s → 0.13s, elementwise 0.18s → 0.06s).

## Validation

- Language suite: 1168 passed, 137 skipped; reducer_v2 suite: 75 passed; arith suite: 89 passed.
- All 17 downstream reducer kernels compile and pass numerics, including three whose layout inference genuinely depends on Z3 proofs.
- Generated CUDA byte-identical to the eager build under disabled ASLR (the only ASLR-dependent deltas are AllReduce workspace slot permutations from a pre-existing pointer-order nondeterminism in shared-memory planning — independent issue).

## Merge order

Depends on tile-ai/tvm#68. The submodule currently points at the PR branch commit (`ea9f9b426`) so CI can validate; once the tvm PR is squash-merged, the pointer here will be updated to the merged SHA before this lands.

title: [ROCm] Remove the Composable Kernel dependency
body:
## Summary

TileLang's only uses of Composable Kernel were a handful of lightweight `ck_tile` utilities in the HIP runtime templates — the type `int32x4_t`, the `CK_TILE_DEVICE` macro, the `CK_TILE_BUFFER_RESOURCE_3RD_DWORD` constant, and `ck_tile::max/min`. GEMM on AMD already goes through `__builtin_amdgcn_mfma_*` intrinsics directly, so no CK device kernels were ever involved. This PR inlines local equivalents and removes the dependency entirely.

### Template changes (`src/tl_templates/hip/`)

- **copy.h**: define `int32x4_t` locally (`ext_vector_type(4)`, needed for `.x/.y/.z/.w` access) and expand CK's arch-grouping macros into an explicit per-gfx `TL_BUFFER_RESOURCE_3RD_DWORD` (`gfx9* = 0x00020000`, `gfx103* = 0x31014000`, `gfx11*/gfx12* = 0x31004000`, host pass `0xffffffff` — matching CK's `config.hpp`)
- **common.h**: drop `#include <ck_tile/core.hpp>`; add `tl::max/min` scalar helpers whose float/double overloads use `__builtin_fmaxf/fminf` to preserve the IEEE NaN semantics (and `v_max3` fusion opportunity) that `ck_tile::max/min` provided
- **ldsm.h / reduce.h / scan.h**: `CK_TILE_DEVICE` → `TL_DEVICE`, `ck_tile::max/min` → `tl::max/min`

### Build / packaging

- `tilelang/env.py`: remove the `TL_COMPOSABLE_KERNEL_PATH` plumbing
- `tilelang/rocm/backend.py`, `tilelang/jit/adapter/libgen.py`: drop the CK `-I` hipcc flags (the template include path was already added separately)
- `pyproject.toml`: stop vendoring `3rdparty/composable_kernel/{include,library}` into the sdist and wheel — a real size win
- `.gitmodules`: remove the submodule, so fresh clones no longer fetch CK

## Testing

- `import tilelang` and an end-to-end CUDA JIT kernel (compile + numerical check, cache disabled) pass; `TL_COMPOSABLE_KERNEL_PATH` no longer appears in the environment
- The replacement constructs (vector type, buffer-resource macro, async buffer loads, max/min overloads) were syntax-checked as HIP device code with clang 18 for gfx942, gfx90a, and gfx1100, confirming the buffer-resource dword resolves to the correct per-arch value

title: [CI] Cap torch<2.14 for CUDA tests until flash-attn supports torch 2.14
body:
## Why

The self-hosted CUDA job started failing in `Setup venv` (e.g. [this run](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/actions/runs/33594121983/job/100134195979)):

1. `torch==2.14.0+cu130` was published on the cu130 index (the last green main run on 8/30 still resolved `2.13.0+cu130`), and its headers now require **C++20**.
2. The pinned `flash-attn==2.5.8` has no prebuilt wheel for torch 2.14 (its `setup.py` wheel-URL guess gets HTTP 404), so it falls back to a source build.
3. The source build compiles with `-std=c++17` and dies with ~100 errors in `c10/core/SymBool.h` (`#error C++20 or later compatible compiler is required`, `std::strong_ordering`, `requires`, ...).
4. The post-failure cleanup then wipes the runner's uv cache, so every retry rebuilds from a cold cache and hits the same wall.

Upgrading flash-attn does not help today: every release up to `2.8.3.post1` — and even upstream `main` — still compiles the **CUDA** extension with `-std=c++17` (only the ROCm/CK path was bumped to C++20), and the newest cu13 prebuilt wheels only cover `torch2.9`. There is no upstream issue/PR for torch 2.14 yet.

## What

Cap `torch<2.14` in `requirements-test-cuda.txt`, next to the flash-attn pin, with a comment stating the removal condition. The current CI matrix has no `Nightly-*` toolkit entries, and ROCm/Metal jobs (both green on torch 2.14) are unaffected.

Note: in the CUDA job, the earlier `uv pip install -r requirements-test.txt` still resolves torch 2.14 before the CUDA requirements downgrade it to 2.13, costing one extra cached torch install (~1-2 min warm). Scoping the cap to the CUDA file was chosen over holding all platforms back; feel free to hoist it into `requirements-test.txt` if you'd rather avoid the double install.

## Revert condition

Remove the cap once a flash-attn release builds its CUDA extension with `-std=c++20` (or ships torch-2.14 wheels).

title: [BugFix][ROCm] Resolve hipcc robustly instead of trusting bare PATH lookup
body:
## Summary

TileLang invokes `hipcc` straight from PATH (`compile_hip` and the JIT library generator), and `find_rocm_path()` derives the ROCm root from `which hipcc`. Partial HIP toolchains without the public headers exist in the wild — e.g. the preview compiler that some ROCm 7 installs prepend to PATH via `/etc/profile.d/rocm.sh` (`/opt/rocm/core-7.14/bin/hipcc`, whose clang only searches `core-7.14/include`, which has no `hip/` subtree). On such hosts every TileLang kernel fails with:

```
fatal error: 'hip/hip_runtime.h' file not found
```

even though a complete install sits right there at `/opt/rocm`. Since the Linux wheel is a fat CUDA+ROCm wheel, this is the first thing a ROCm user can hit after `pip install tilelang`. Our own CI already works around it by prepending `/opt/rocm/bin` to PATH.

## Fix

Add `find_hipcc()` to `tilelang.contrib.rocm` with the following resolution order:

1. `$ROCM_PATH/bin/hipcc` — an explicit `ROCM_PATH` is honored as-is;
2. every `hipcc` on PATH, in PATH order;
3. `/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc`.

Candidates from 2 and 3 are accepted only when their toolchain prefix carries the public HIP headers (`include/hip/hip_runtime.h`), following symlinks so versioned installs (`/opt/rocm -> /opt/rocm-x.y`) validate against the real prefix. Skipped candidates log a one-shot warning. If no candidate validates, the first existing one is returned so the compiler reports its own error (legacy behavior preserved).

`compile_hip` and `LibraryGenerator` now invoke the resolved executable, and `find_rocm_path()`, `env.ROCM_HOME`, and `check_hip_availability()` share the same validated resolution (`tilelang/contrib/hipcc.py` also switches from `tvm.contrib.rocm` to the hardened tilelang helpers).

## Testing

- MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.0.2) host with the broken preview toolchain first on PATH: GEMM JIT + correctness now pass with the stock environment (previously required PATH surgery); `ROCM_PATH` override and clean-PATH runs unchanged.
- H100 (CUDA) regression: unaffected.

title: [CI] Fix slow Windows wheel builds by making ccache effective
body:
## Summary

The `Dist` workflow's Windows wheel job takes ~48 min while Linux takes ~9 min (see e.g. [run 33572214431](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/actions/runs/33572214431)). Almost all of it is cibuildwheel recompiling all ~700 TVM + TileLang TUs with clang-cl on every run: the ccache hit rate was **8/698 (1.15%)** on Windows vs **678/714 (95%)** on Linux.

## Root causes

1. **PEP 517 build-isolation tempdir names leak into ccache's hash.** cibuildwheel's `build` frontend materializes each build into a randomly-named `Temp\build-env-XXXXXXXX` dir, which hosts the pip-provided CUDA cu13 / z3 headers. That path is preserved in the preprocessor output as `#line` directives, so ccache's preprocessed-mode result key changes on every run. The repo already ships the fix — `cmake/ccache_strip_pep517.py`, plugged in via ccache `prefix_command_cpp` — but:
   - CMakeLists.txt only activates it when a stable interpreter exists at `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`, and CI never created one (the configure log shows `ccache: no stable .venv python found`);
   - the wrapper's regex only matched uv's `.tmpXXX` naming, not the `build-env-XXX` naming pypa/build actually uses (nor random suffixes containing `_`, e.g. `build-env-gna_6ikk`).
2. **`max-size: 200MB` is smaller than one full build's output.** ccache evicted entries mid-build (522 cleanups, cache 99.96% full), so the cache could never converge to a full set of objects.

The command-line side is already safe: ccache 4.9 natively treats `-imsvc` / `-external:I` as preprocessor path options excluded from the cpp-mode hash, so the `#line` text was the only leak.

## Changes

- `cmake/ccache_strip_pep517.py`: widen normalization to `(?:\.tmp|build-env-|cibw-run-)[A-Za-z0-9_]+`. The rewritten text is only hashed, never compiled, so this cannot miscompile.
- `.github/workflows/dist.yml`: move `setup-uv` before the build step and create a repo-root `.venv` on Windows so the wrapper activates; raise ccache `max-size` to 2GB for the wheel jobs.
- `CMakeLists.txt`: suppress clang-cl's `-Wdelayed-template-parsing-in-cxx20` deprecation warning (feature-checked so older LLVM doesn't emit unknown-warning-option noise instead); it fired on every C++20 TU and flooded the logs.

## Expected effect / how to verify

The first Windows run after this lands still compiles cold (~45 min) and populates the cache. Subsequent runs should hit ~95% and drop "Build wheels" from ~44 min to well under 10 min. Check the `Post Setup ccache` stats and the `ccache: stripping PEP 517 .tmpXXX paths via ...` configure line (instead of `no stable .venv python found`).

Since this PR touches `dist.yml` / `CMakeLists.txt`, the Dist workflow runs on the PR itself — the second datapoint needs a re-run or a follow-up push.
